title: The frontend's CPH example teaches a 3/3/3 grouping that no CPH number uses; DR1's example is 12/345/6789.

finding.frontend: The hint under the single input reads "For example, 123456789 or 123/456/789." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/copy/copy.en.js:5), and fe-cph-number renders it directly above the box. A county parish holding number is two digits of county, three of parish and four of holding, so the second example teaches a grouping that does not exist. The mistake never surfaces in testing because the controller strips the slashes before counting digits (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:77), so a trader who copies the pattern still passes validation — the only casualty is the trader who now believes their number is wrongly formatted, or who transcribes it into the wrong grouping elsewhere.
finding.prototype: DR1 hints the same question with "For example 12/345/6789" (app/views/partials/cph-number-input.html:14), placed above all three boxes so it explains the whole number rather than any one part. The 2/3/4 shape it teaches is the shape the three boxes enforce through their widths and maxlengths (:21,33,45).
finding.difference: Change the example to the real grouping, "For example 12/345/6789". Keep the unslashed alternative only if content design wants it, and if so make it consistent with the grouping. Nothing about validation changes: the controller already accepts both forms.
finding.falsifiedBy: APHA publishing CPH numbers in a 3/3/3 grouping, which would make the frontend's example right and DR1's wrong.

relatedTo.why: the grouping the hint should teach is the grouping the three boxes would enforce
